# Debrief: Argo CD, Prometheus

These clips cover Argo CD practices: keeping Helm values in Git, previewing pull request changes with a real Argo CD instance, and using Argo CD's API for troubleshooting; Prometheus appears only as a passing mention. ([Declarative...ish? Fixing Hidden Argo CD Pitfalls in Your GitOps Setup · 5:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VfVQj4Oa3z0&t=339s); [Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 5:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=326s); [The 10x DevOps Engineer’s Toolkit: Argo CD + AI-Driven MCP Automation · 15:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iC15zeOLZQA&t=924s))

## Top 3 takeaways

1. Store Helm settings in Helm value files in Git and have the Argo CD application reference them, separating business settings from where applications are deployed, and keeping local runs with staging settings simple. ([Declarative...ish? Fixing Hidden Argo CD Pitfalls in Your GitOps Setup · 5:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VfVQj4Oa3z0&t=339s))
2. Rendering pull request changes with a real Argo CD instance matches production configuration. The main downside is speed, since creating a cluster and installing Argo CD to process many applications takes time. ([Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 5:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=326s))
3. One team cut pull request rendering from half an hour to 3 minutes with watch patterns, then to 30 seconds by using a pre-configured cluster, rendering only what changed. ([Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 17:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=1039s))

## Action items

- [ ] Audit your Argo CD applications for Helm parameters defined inline in manifests, and move them into Helm value files in Git referenced from the application source. ([Declarative...ish? Fixing Hidden Argo CD Pitfalls in Your GitOps Setup · 5:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VfVQj4Oa3z0&t=339s))
- [ ] Prototype a pull request preview that renders manifests with a real Argo CD instance, then try watch patterns and a pre-configured cluster to cut render time. ([Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 5:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=326s); [Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 17:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=1039s))
- [ ] Evaluate pulling application logs, Kubernetes events, and live versus desired state from the Argo CD API to reduce data spread across tools such as Prometheus-based dashboards. ([The 10x DevOps Engineer’s Toolkit: Argo CD + AI-Driven MCP Automation · 15:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iC15zeOLZQA&t=924s))

## Watch together (7 min)

1. [Declarative...ish? Fixing Hidden Argo CD Pitfalls in Your GitOps Setup · 5:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VfVQj4Oa3z0&t=339s) (1:20), Regina Voloshin: Concrete best practice for Helm values and Argo CD manifests.
2. [Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 5:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=326s) (1:18), Dag Bjerre Andersen, Sergey Shevchenko: Explains previewing pull request changes with a real Argo CD instance.
3. [Argo CD: Previewing Pull Request Changes in SECONDS! · 17:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcajag5di68&t=1039s) (1:19), Dag Bjerre Andersen, Sergey Shevchenko: Shows measured speedups from watch patterns and pre-configured clusters.
4. [The 10x DevOps Engineer’s Toolkit: Argo CD + AI-Driven MCP Automation · 15:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iC15zeOLZQA&t=924s) (1:19), Alexander Matyushentsev, Leonardo Luz Almeida: Argo CD API as a way to unify troubleshooting data.
5. [The 10x DevOps Engineer’s Toolkit: Argo CD + AI-Driven MCP Automation · 18:44](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iC15zeOLZQA&t=1124s) (1:19), Alexander Matyushentsev, Leonardo Luz Almeida: Honest lesson on low adoption of an AI troubleshooting button.
